title: Are more prisoners leaving with a working electronic tag?
scope: England and Wales, electronic monitoring after release from prison
reader: A reader of the existing tagging guide checking whether prison fitting addresses gaps in monitoring after release.
primaryAngle: Follow the promised fitting figures and compare whether people leave with working tags, using matching cohorts and definitions.
secondaryAngle: Distinguish announced prison coverage, fitted tags, functioning monitoring and any evidence of the delay between release and monitoring.
lastingValue: The existing guide tracks the delivery test, so new comparable information updates an established public record.

signals.detail: The 26 November 2026 PAC hearing is already covered in the guide, which records a commitment to publish updated fitting figures in January 2027.
The Ministry of Justice published a staged plan to expand fitting in prisons on 25 November 2026.

hearing.title: Electronic Monitoring: follow-up, oral evidence
hearing.publisher: House of Commons Public Accounts Committee
hearing.locator: 26 November 2026 session. Use the timestamped fitting-figures exchange already recorded in the guide when checking the wording of the promise.

rollout.title: Thousands more tags to be fitted in prison in major expansion
rollout.locator: Rollout timetable and pilot. Treat the timetable as a plan unless delivery is evidenced.

status-figures.title: Electronic monitoring status statistics, September 2026
status-figures.locator: Tables 6.1 and 6.2 in the existing guide. Check their populations before using them as a baseline for new fitting data.

usefulness.reason: Whether monitoring starts at release changes how readers should understand the service’s protection.

urgency.reason: The published commitment gives January 2027, with a check planned early in that month.

coverage.reason: Deepens an existing part of the justice catalogue.

evidence.reason: There is a recorded promise and baseline evidence. The expected fitting release still needs verification.

evidenceGap: A release giving the number of prisons covered or tags fitted may still leave unanswered how many people left prison with a working tag and how long others went unmonitored.
draftingChecks: Reopen the committee publications, transcript or recording and MoJ releases when the check is due.
Establish the exact cohort, period and stages reported as releases, fittings and monitoring starts. Compare with like-for-like published baseline figures.
Append a dated entry to the existing fitting-figures follow-up if information is provided or partly provided. Put any actual delivery change beside the fitting finding.

nextCheck.what: Look for the promised January publication in PAC correspondence and MoJ statistics. The exact day is an editorial check, since the commitment specified a month.

refresh.change: The current guide already covers the hearing and rollout announcement. Wait for the promised fitting data or another materially relevant record.
refresh.impact: Readers could see whether the expansion closes the gap between release and effective monitoring, and whether the published evidence can answer the question.

decisionReason: Hold until the publisher supplies new evidence. The hearing and announcement by themselves would repeat existing coverage.
